requirements.original: int2str(in integer invalue) return charstring
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2str` has the signature `int2str(in integer invalue) return charstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.7 -- int2str(in integer invalue) return charstring

requirements.original: This function converts the integer value into its string equivalent (the base of the return string is always decimal).
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2str` converts an integer value into the charstring representing that value.

examples.text:
int2str(66)  // will return the charstring value "66"
  int2str(-66)  // will return the charstring value "-66"
  int2str(0)  // will return the charstring value "0"

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.7 -- This function converts the integer value into its string equivalent (the base of the return string is always decimal).

requirements.original: This function converts the integer value into its string equivalent (the base of the return string is always decimal).
requirements.canonical: The charstring returned by `int2str` IS always the decimal representation of the integer value.

examples.text:
int2str(66)  // will return the charstring value "66"
  int2str(-66)  // will return the charstring value "-66"
  int2str(0)  // will return the charstring value "0"

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.7 -- This function converts the integer value into its string equivalent (the base of the return string is always decimal).

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2str`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.7 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: float2int(in float invalue) return integer
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `float2int` has the signature `float2int(in float invalue) return integer`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.9 -- float2int(in float invalue) return integer

requirements.original: This function converts a float value into an integer value by removing the fractional part of the argument and returning the resulting integer.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `float2int` converts a float value into an integer value by removing the fractional part of the argument and returning the resulting integer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.9 -- This function converts a float value into an integer value by removing the fractional part of the argument and returning the resulting integer.

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `float2int`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.9 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: invalue is infinity, -infinity or not_a_number. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is `infinity`, `-infinity` or `not_a_number`, the call of `float2int` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.9 -- invalue is infinity, -infinity or not_a_number. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: char2int(in charstring invalue) return integer
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `char2int` has the signature `char2int(in charstring invalue) return integer`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.10 -- char2int(in charstring invalue) return integer

requirements.original: This function converts a single-character-length charstring value into an integer value in the range of 0 to 127.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `char2int` converts a single-character-length charstring value into an integer value in the range 0 to 127.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.10 -- This function converts a single-character-length charstring value into an integer value in the range of 0 to 127.

requirements.original: The integer value describes the 8-bit encoding of the character.
requirements.canonical: The integer value returned by `char2int` IS the encoding (character code) of the character in `invalue`.

ambiguity.issue: The range 0..127 corresponds to a 7-bit character code; the text calls it an 8-bit encoding.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.10 -- The integer value describes the 8-bit encoding of the character.

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `char2int`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.10 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: length of invalue does not equal 1. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: If the length of `invalue` is not 1, the call of `char2int` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.10 -- length of invalue does not equal 1. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: char2oct(in charstring invalue) return octetstring
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `char2oct` has the signature `char2oct(in charstring invalue) return octetstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.11 -- char2oct(in charstring invalue) return octetstring

requirements.original: This function converts a charstring invalue to an octetstring.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `char2oct` converts a charstring `invalue` into an octetstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.11 -- This function converts a charstring invalue to an octetstring.

requirements.original: Each octet of the octetstring will contain the Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] codes (according to the IRV) of the appropriate characters of invalue.
requirements.canonical: Each octet of the octetstring returned by `char2oct` contains the Recommendation ITU-T T.50 code (according to the IRV) of the corresponding character of `invalue`, in the same order.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.11 -- Each octet of the octetstring will contain the Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] codes (according to the IRV) of the appropriate characters of invalue.

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `char2oct`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.11 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.12 -- This function converts a single-character-length universal charstring value into an integer value in the range of 0 to 2 147 483 647.

requirements.original: The integer value describes the 32-bit encoding of the character.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.12 -- The integer value describes the 32-bit encoding of the character.

requirements.original: bit2int(in bitstring invalue) return integer
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `bit2int` has the signature `bit2int(in bitstring invalue) return integer`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- bit2int(in bitstring invalue) return integer

requirements.original: This function converts a single bitstring value to a single integer value.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `bit2int` converts a single bitstring value into a single integer value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- This function converts a single bitstring value to a single integer value.

requirements.original: For the purposes of this conversion, a bitstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.
requirements.canonical: For the conversion performed by `bit2int`, the bitstring SHALL be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.

ambiguity.issue: The value 0 is a valid result/argument, so the bitstring is interpreted as a non-negative (not strictly positive) integer.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- For the purposes of this conversion, a bitstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.

requirements.original: The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `bit2int`, the rightmost bit IS the least significant bit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.

requirements.original: The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `bit2int`, the leftmost bit IS the most significant bit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.

requirements.original: The bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `bit2int`, the bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- The bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `bit2int`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.13 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: bit2hex(in bitstring invalue) return hexstring
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `bit2hex` has the signature `bit2hex(in bitstring invalue) return hexstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- bit2hex(in bitstring invalue) return hexstring

requirements.original: This function converts a single bitstring value to a single hexstring.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `bit2hex` converts a single bitstring value into a single hexstring value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- This function converts a single bitstring value to a single hexstring.

requirements.original: The resulting hexstring represents the same value as the bitstring.
requirements.canonical: The hexstring returned by `bit2hex` represents the same value as the bitstring `invalue`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- The resulting hexstring represents the same value as the bitstring.

requirements.original: For the purpose of this conversion, a bitstring shall be converted into a hexstring, where the bitstring is divided into groups of four bits beginning with the rightmost bit.
requirements.canonical: For the conversion performed by `bit2hex`, the bitstring SHALL be divided into groups of four bits beginning with the rightmost bit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- For the purpose of this conversion, a bitstring shall be converted into a hexstring, where the bitstring is divided into groups of four bits beginning with the rightmost bit.

requirements.canonical: `bit2hex` SHALL convert each group of four bits into one hexadecimal digit according to the mapping '0000'B to '0'H, '0001'B to '1'H, ..., '1110'B to 'E'H and '1111'B to 'F'H (the hexadecimal digit whose value equals the base 2 value of the group).

requirements.original: When the leftmost group of bits does contain less than 4 bits, this group is filled with '0'B from the left until it contains exactly 4 bits and is converted afterwards.
requirements.canonical: If the leftmost group of bits contains fewer than 4 bits, `bit2hex` SHALL fill that group with '0'B from the left until it contains exactly 4 bits before converting it.
requirements.condition: the length of invalue is not a multiple of 4
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- When the leftmost group of bits does contain less than 4 bits, this group is filled with '0'B from the left until it contains exactly 4 bits and is converted afterwards.

requirements.original: The consecutive order of hex digits in the resulting hexstring is the same as the order of groups of 4 bits in the bitstring.
requirements.canonical: The order of hexadecimal digits in the hexstring returned by `bit2hex` IS the same as the order of the groups of 4 bits in the bitstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- The consecutive order of hex digits in the resulting hexstring is the same as the order of groups of 4 bits in the bitstring.

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `bit2hex`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.14 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
